content:
Hark hark good soul who dost embark on journey to fair Japan
Let mine words be thy guide through days so bright ane black
Upon the morn of thy first day thou shalt alight in Tokyo’s embrace
Where lanterns glow like stars in twilight’s tender grasp

Behold the sun doth rise o’er Mount Fuji’s lofty height
Thy first morn shall be spent in Asakusa’s sacred light
Where temples stand in reverence old as time’s own breath
And Kannon’s grace doth fill the air with whispers soft and sweet

To Senso-ji’s halls thou shalt make thy way with heart sincere
Where bell’s chimes ring like angels’ voices clear and pure
Walk through Nakamise’s stall where treasures old and new are sold
Silken fans and sweets of earthly joy to please thy soul’s behold

Come midday’s hour when hunger doth thy spirit claim
Seek out Tsukiji’s market where the sea’s bounty doth proclaim
Fresh fish still glistening bright as morning’s first dew
Sashimi fit for kings and grilled delights to make thy taste buds new

When eve doth fall and shadows creep like ghosts of yore
Make thy way to Shinjuku where neon lights do dance and soar
Golden Gai’s alleys twist like labyrinths of old
With bars and izakayas where laughter rings both loud and bold

On morn’s return thou shalt depart this lively den of cheer
To Kyoto’s ancient streets where history doth whisper near
Fushimi Inari’s torii gates stretch far as eye can see
A crimson path to heaven’s gate where foxes watch thee flee

Nijo Castle’s golden shores reflect thy weary tread
Where samurai once did stride with swords that gleamed like bread
Kinkaku-ji’s hall of gold doth blind the eyes with light divine
A gilded dream where time itself doth seem to pause and shine

The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove shall make thy heart take flight
Where winds do weave through stalks so tall and straight and bright
Monkey Park’s mischievous troops shall steal thy snack away
Yet grin with cheeky charm that robs thy sorrow all its sway

On third morn’s dawn thou shalt arise with vigor fresh and keen
To Nara’s sacred grounds where deer do wander free and lean
Todai-ji’s giant Buddha sits in quiet majesty
His gaze both kind and wise upon the world’s eternity

Feed the deer with crackers bought from stalls so sweet
Their nimble leaps and bounds shall bring joy that cannot be beat
Then wander Kasuga’s paths where lanterns hang in rows
Like stars plucked from the sky to light thy way through rows

When night doth fall and stars above do twinkle soft and low
Return to Kyoto’s heart where Gion’s lanterns gently glow
Hanamikoji’s bridge doth hum with geisha’s secret tread
And teahouses whisper tales of love both fierce and fed

On fifth morn’s break of day thou shalt take heed and rise
To Osaka’s bustling streets where castles stand with might and size
Osaka Castle’s stone walls bear scars of battles long ago
Yet stand in grandeur proud where merchants come and go

Dotonbori’s neon signs reflect upon the river’s face
Where takoyaki balls are cooked with love and fiery grace
Street foods of every kind shall tantalize thy taste
From kushikatsu sticks to okonomiyaki’s savory feast

To Universal Studios thou shalt make thy way anew
Where Super Nintendo World shall make thy inner child break through
Ride the rollercoasters high where thrills shall fill the air
And Harry Potter’s magic cast a spell beyond compare

On sixth morn’s dawn thy journey’s end doth draw quite near
To Hiroshima’s sobering gates where peace doth stand sincere
Parks of solemn stillness hold the past’s grave weight
Yet life persists with flowers bright in memory’s gentle mate

The Atomic Bomb Dome stands as grim and haunting sight
A warning carved in stone of war’s cruel bitter night
Yet children’s laughter rings in Miyajima’s holy air
Where Itsukushima’s shrine doth rise from waters calm and fair

On final morn thou shalt arise with heart both full and light
To Tokyo’s gleaming towers where thy journey doth take flight
Last-minute souvenirs from Depachika’s foodie hall
Where flavors rich and decadent tempt thy final call

Before thy flight homeward bound where modern meets the old
Stand one last time where Shinjuku’s skyscrapers stand cold
Yet in thy soul Japan’s spirit shall forever burn so bright
A land of contrasts fierce where ancient walks with light.
